engines.NAME: llama.cpp
engines.WHAT: The reference GGUF runtime, with a first-class Metal backend. New architectures land here earlier and more completely than anywhere else on this page, and Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, KoboldCpp and most other local runners are downstream of it. `llama-server` exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so nothing here is GUI-only.

API_DETAIL.endpoints: OpenAI: /v1/models, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings, plus token-counting routes for chat and responses. Anthropic: /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens. Also /slots prompt-cache save/restore, Prometheus /metrics, and real-time completion control.
API_DETAIL.streaming: SSE on every chat surface. Returns a standard `usage` object plus a `timings` block that reports `cache_n` - how many prompt tokens were reused from cache - which is the number you want when tuning an agent loop.
API_DETAIL.tools: Native tool-call styles per model family with a generic fallback, `tool_choice`, and `parallel_tool_calls` gated on what the jinja template supports. Arguments stream as deltas.
API_DETAIL.structured: `response_format` accepts both `json_object` and `json_schema`, enforced by GBNF grammar sampling at the token level rather than validated afterwards.
API_DETAIL.concurrency: Parallel slots (`-np`), with per-slot prompt caches you can persist to disk.
API_DETAIL.gotcha: Tool use requires the `--jinja` flag on both the OpenAI and Anthropic surfaces - without it `tools` is silently inert. The project's own docs decline to claim spec compliance: “no strong claims of compatibility with OpenAI API spec is being made”.

engines.NAME: Ollama
engines.FORMAT: MLX on Apple Silicon, GGUF elsewhere
engines.WHAT: One-command pulls from a curated library, running as a launch-agent server. Since v0.30 (May 2026) MLX is the default engine on Apple Silicon rather than llama.cpp, which is the single most important thing to know about it here: on a Mac, Ollama inherits MLX's architecture coverage for the models it serves through that path.

API_DETAIL.endpoints: OpenAI: /v1/models, /v1/models/{model}, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/responses. Anthropic-compatible surface as well. Its own richer /api/* routes sit alongside.
API_DETAIL.streaming: Yes, with `stream_options`. The only engine here that publishes an explicit checkbox matrix of what it does and does not implement, which is worth more than most of the feature lists.
API_DETAIL.tools: Tools yes, but **`tool_choice` is not implemented** - you cannot force a specific call or require that one happen. Also missing: `logprobs`, `n`, `logit_bias`, `user`.
API_DETAIL.concurrency: Serves concurrently with automatic model loading and unloading.
API_DETAIL.gotcha: `/v1/responses` is non-stateful only: no `previous_response_id`, no `conversation`. And because MLX is now the default engine on Apple Silicon, a tag can resolve to a different backend than you expect.

engines.NAME: LM Studio

RELEASE_FEED.note: closed source; no public tag feed, see the in-app release notes

engines.WHAT: App-first but not app-only. It ships both a llama.cpp engine and its own MLX engine, so for any given model it can take whichever path works, and its catalogue tends to carry a curated quant within a day of a release. The `lms` CLI and the server run headless.

API_DETAIL.endpoints: OpenAI: /v1/models, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings. Its own REST API and TypeScript/Python SDKs are more capable than the compatibility layer.
API_DETAIL.streaming: Yes. Tool calls stream properly as `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments` fragments you accumulate across chunks - the correct OpenAI shape.
API_DETAIL.tools: Standard OpenAI tool schemas, with per-family native formats and a documented generic fallback for models with no native tool support.
API_DETAIL.structured: `json_schema` only - **`json_object` mode is not supported**. Enforcement differs by engine: llama.cpp grammars for GGUF, Outlines for MLX. SDK integrations bind to Zod, Pydantic and msgspec.
API_DETAIL.concurrency: Serves multiple requests; models load and unload through the app or `lms`.
API_DETAIL.gotcha: The two engines are not equivalent through the same API. An open report has the MLX engine silently clamping context to 4864 tokens and ignoring every override, which surfaces as the model being bad rather than the server being wrong.

engines.NAME: oMLX
engines.WHAT: MLX serving built for agent clients: continuous batching, a hot/cold KV cache that spills blocks to SSD and survives a restart, and hand-written Metal kernels for the GLM-5.2, MiniMax M3 and Qwen3.5 families. Its LLM coverage is mlx-lm's, plus those kernels and its own additions - install the custom kernels or the affected families fall back silently to a much slower generic path.

API_DETAIL.streaming: Yes, including `stream_options.include_usage`, and SSE keep-alives so a long prefill does not read-timeout the client. It also scales reported token counts so Claude Code's auto-compact triggers at the right moment on a smaller-context model.
API_DETAIL.tools: Per-family parsers (Qwen3.5 XML, GLM arg-key/value, MiniMax namespaced, Gemma, Kimi, Mistral, Longcat). **Tool calls do not stream incrementally** - assistant text streams while tool markup is suppressed, and structured calls are emitted only after the completed turn is parsed.
API_DETAIL.structured: JSON schema validation, plus MCP tool integration.
API_DETAIL.concurrency: Continuous batching, default 8 concurrent requests, over a hot/cold KV cache that spills to SSD and survives a restart.
API_DETAIL.gotcha: The two surfaces are not interchangeable in practice: there is an open report of the OpenAI endpoint returning 500 while the Anthropic endpoint on the same server works. A stricter channel check also drops valid gpt-oss calls addressed to `functions.*`.

engines.NAME: vLLM Metal

RELEASE_FEED.note: v0.28.0 on 2026-09-01 is the first non-prerelease since v0.2.0 in June; the version now tracks vLLM upstream rather than the plugin

engines.WHAT: vLLM itself, running on Apple Silicon. This is a plugin in the vllm-project org that keeps vLLM core and swaps the compute layer for MLX, unifying MLX and PyTorch under one lowering path - so you get vLLM's scheduler, paged KV, continuous batching and API surface rather than a lookalike. Despite the name it is an MLX engine underneath: it pins a single exact MLX version, pulls in mlx-lm and mlx-vlm, and builds its Metal kernels as MLX primitives. Two things make it worth attention on new hardware: v0.2.0's unified paged varlen Metal kernel claims 83x TTFT and 3.6x throughput over v0.1.0, and as of August 2026 it uses the **M5 Neural Accelerator tensor units** to speed up MHA, GQA and MQA prefill - the only engine here that claims M5-specific acceleration. The cost is coverage: its model matrix is a curated list, not everything that exists.

API_DETAIL.endpoints: Whatever vLLM core exposes, because this is vLLM: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/models, plus the pooling and rerank routes for the embedding and reranker models it supports.
API_DETAIL.streaming: vLLM's own implementation rather than a reimplementation, so streaming, usage accounting and the rest behave the way the upstream docs say they do.
API_DETAIL.tools: vLLM's tool parsers and guided decoding, again inherited from core. One live defect to know about: mixed batches with top_k enabled on some requests and disabled on others crash the Metal sampler.
API_DETAIL.concurrency: Continuous batching and paged KV from vLLM core, over Metal kernels. Automatic prefix caching is on by default for unified paged-KV models; hybrid GDN models like Qwen3.8 must opt in with --enable-prefix-caching.
API_DETAIL.gotcha: Model coverage is far narrower than llama.cpp's - this is a young plugin with a deliberately curated matrix, not a general loader. Check the supported-models table before planning around it. Needs macOS 15+ and native arm64 Python 3.12 specifically. And note the MLX pin is exact, not a floor: the prebuilt kernels link MLX private headers and libmlx.dylib carries no SONAME version, so a wheel is only ABI-safe against the one MLX it was built against. You cannot upgrade MLX underneath it.

engines.NAME: vllm-mlx
engines.WHAT: A paged KV cache and continuous batching over mlx-lm's model classes. Unaffiliated with vllm-project/vllm despite the name. Because it wraps mlx-lm rather than reimplementing models, an architecture missing upstream is missing here, and mlx-lm's bugs arrive intact.

API_DETAIL.endpoints: OpenAI: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank, /v1/responses. Anthropic: /v1/messages with streaming, tool use and system prompts. Prometheus /metrics.
API_DETAIL.streaming: Yes on both surfaces. Usage is reported, but `cached_tokens` is not surfaced yet - an open PR - so you cannot see prefix-cache hits from the API.
API_DETAIL.tools: 19 tool parsers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma and more) plus reasoning parsers selected with `--reasoning-parser`.
API_DETAIL.concurrency: The strongest story on paper: continuous batching over a paged KV cache with prefix caching and SSD tiering, which is the whole reason the project exists.
API_DETAIL.gotcha: Three open defects land squarely on the streaming path: streamed tool calls can end without a `finish_reason`, closing a stream mid-flight leaves the generator and request state open, and a strict `json_schema` decode can wedge. Also bind carefully - non-loopback requests have been reported silently dropped on 0.0.0.0.

engines.NAME: mlx-lm
engines.WHAT: Apple's own reference implementation, and the substrate almost everything MLX-shaped depends on. Treat it as the floor: an architecture with no model class here is absent from most of the MLX ecosystem at once. The bundled server is deliberately basic - one model, simple batching - so it is a correctness reference more than a serving layer.

API_DETAIL.endpoints: OpenAI: POST /v1/chat/completions (and bare /chat/completions), POST /v1/completions, GET /v1/models, GET /health. No embeddings, no rerank, no responses.
API_DETAIL.streaming: Yes, SSE, with `stream_options.include_usage` and `prompt_tokens_details` for cached prompt tokens.
API_DETAIL.tools: `tool_calls` are parsed and returned. It also implements `logprobs` and `top_logprobs` up to 11, which Ollama does not - a genuine inversion of the usual ordering.
API_DETAIL.structured: **None.** There is no `response_format`, no `json_schema` and no grammar support anywhere in the server. If your agent depends on constrained decoding, this engine cannot give it to you.
API_DETAIL.concurrency: A ThreadingHTTPServer over mlx-lm's BatchGenerator, but batching is switched off whenever a draft model is loaded or a `seed` is set - so speculative decoding and concurrency are mutually exclusive here.
API_DETAIL.gotcha: Better than its reputation on the basics and thinner than expected on structured output. Treat it as a correctness reference rather than a serving layer.

engines.NAME: DwarfStar (ds4)

RELEASE_FEED.note: untagged by design (ds4#839); build from main

engines.WHAT: A single-purpose C and Metal engine for DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V4 PRO and GLM-5.2 - deliberately not a general GGUF loader, so only the published checkpoints load. In exchange it gets a disk KV cache that persists sessions across restarts, resident session batching, SSD expert streaming for machines too small to hold the weights, and tensor parallelism across two Macs over Thunderbolt RDMA. Where it applies, it is the fastest option here.

API_DETAIL.endpoints: OpenAI: /v1/models, /v1/models/{alias}, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses. Anthropic: /v1/messages. The model aliases are compatibility only - they all report whatever GGUF was passed with `-m`.
API_DETAIL.streaming: SSE on the chat, Responses and Anthropic surfaces, with `stream_options.include_usage`. In thinking mode reasoning streams on its own channel instead of being mixed into the final text, and the Responses surface emits the full Codex event lifecycle - `response.output_text.delta`, function-call argument events, and terminal `response.completed` / `incomplete` / `failed`.
API_DETAIL.tools: `tools` and `tool_choice` on all three surfaces. Schemas are rendered into DeepSeek's DSML format and generated calls mapped back. **Tool calls stream incrementally**: the header goes out as soon as the DSML invocation is recognised, then argument bytes are forwarded as `tool_calls[].function.arguments` deltas while generation continues.
API_DETAIL.structured: No `response_format` or grammar support; correctness comes from DSML canonicalisation rather than constrained decoding.
API_DETAIL.concurrency: `--batched-session N` preallocates N resident KV sessions with fair scheduling, and idle slots persist to the disk KV cache before reuse. MTP speculative decoding is disabled while native session batching is active.
API_DETAIL.gotcha: The best streaming implementation here, from the narrowest engine - but stateless clients have been reported failing to extend the live KV session on Flash/Metal, which quietly removes the prefix reuse that is the main reason to run it. Add `--cors` for browser clients; `--host 0.0.0.0` is opt-in.

engines.NAME: mflux
engines.WHAT: A line-by-line MLX port of a dozen image model families, written from scratch rather than wrapping diffusers - FLUX.2, Z-Image, Qwen Image, Krea 2, Ideogram 4, FIBO and more, plus SeedVR2 for upscaling and Depth Pro for depth. It is deliberately minimal and explicit, and it is the most active image runtime on Apple Silicon by a distance. There is no server: you drive it from the CLI or import it, so putting it behind an API is your job.

engines.NAME: MLX-Audio
engines.WHAT: The centre of gravity for audio on Apple Silicon, and the largest catalogue on this page: twenty-odd TTS families, a similar spread of speech-to-text, speaker diarisation, speech enhancement and music generation. If an audio model has an MLX port at all, this is usually where it lives.

engines.NAME: MLX-Video
engines.WHAT: Inference and finetuning for image, video and audio generation models. Same author as MLX-Audio. Worth checking the commit history before planning around it - it moves in bursts rather than continuously.

engines.NAME: DiffusionKit
engines.WHAT: Argmax's on-device image generation for Apple Silicon, covering both MLX and Core ML. Solid engineering, but it has not been touched since April 2025, so it predates every model added to this page and should be treated as a reference implementation rather than a live option.

51.headline: Add support for LTX-2.5
51.why: LTX-2.5 is the current Lightricks video model and MLX weights for it are already published, but mlx-video only implements LTX-2 and LTX-2.3. Until this lands, the newest weights have no loader in this engine.

805.headline: Disk KV cache can be reused across different weights sharing a model_id
805.why: Swap quantisations and the cache from the old weights can be restored against the new ones. Silent wrong-context, and it survives a restart because that is what the disk cache is for.

807.headline: DeepSeek V4 PRO 0813 support
807.why: The 0813 refresh is not yet a supported checkpoint. ds4 is deliberately narrow, so a newer PRO release is a tracked task rather than something that just loads.

816.headline: Stateless chat clients never extend the live KV session on Flash/Metal
816.why: Most agent clients are stateless - they resend a longer prompt each turn. If the session is not extended, the disk KV cache and prefix reuse stop paying, which is the main reason to run ds4.

836.headline: Possible ds4-server memory leak
836.why: Unconfirmed. On a machine where the model already occupies most of RAM, a slow server-side leak ends as an OOM rather than as swap.

839.headline: No tagged releases, which blocks downstream packaging
839.why: You build from a moving main branch. The project describes itself as beta and fast-changing, so pin a commit yourself if you care about reproducibility.

845.headline: --layers maps a shard as N disjoint Metal buffers, about 77x slower decode
845.why: Hits the distributed path specifically. If you are splitting DeepSeek V4 PRO or GLM-5.2 across two Macs, this is the first thing to check when the numbers look impossible.

851.headline: DeepSeek V4 Flash vision is not supported
851.why: Text only today. Irrelevant for coding and terminal work; relevant if you wanted the same engine for screenshots.

853.headline: BPE merge loop is O(n squared): large prompts take minutes to tokenize
853.why: Tokenization is pure fixed cost before any GPU work. An agent that pastes a file into the prompt pays it on every turn, and it does not show up in the tok/s figures.

860.headline: ds4 crashes the machine on launch for one reporter
860.why: A single report without a resolved cause. Listed because a full-machine crash is a different risk class from a process crash.

27742.headline: model: add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp)
27742.why: Merged 2026-08-27, which is what unblocked this architecture. It is on master only - no tagged release carries it yet, so a packaged build will not load the weights until the next release cuts.

27752.headline: model: add GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5next)
27752.why: One of three competing open PRs for the same architecture (#27752, #27754, #27773). Quants are already published, so the weights are waiting on whichever of these lands.

25522.headline: Gemma 4 crashes with MTP speculative decoding
25522.why: MTP is the reason to prefer the GGUF build - the checkpoint ships a draft head. With MTP off the model runs, so this costs speed rather than correctness.

25739.headline: Google's own Gemma 4 QAT GGUF aborts at vocab load
25739.why: Closed 2026-09-03 as not planned, which is a decision not to fix rather than a fix - the vocab assert on Google's own QAT GGUF still stands. Filed against the E2B variant, and it matters because the QAT repo is the recommended download, so this is the default path and not an exotic one. Treat the closed marker as 'no longer being worked on'.

25751.headline: Sliding-window attention on Gemma 4 forgets key details
25751.why: Gemma 4's long context is built on SWA, so this bites exactly where the 256k window is the reason you picked the model. Quality loss, not a crash, which makes it harder to notice.

25967.headline: Duplicate GBNF rules with a large tool list break grammar parsing
25967.why: Closed 2026-09-03 as not planned - a decision not to fix rather than a fix, so the defect stands. Constrained decoding is how tool calls are kept well-formed, and past some number of tools the generated grammar fails to parse, which is to say the failure arrives exactly when an agent has enough tools to be useful. Read the closed marker as 'no longer being worked on'.

26365.headline: Kimi K3 full-size vision lives on a branch, not master
26365.why: Closed 2026-09-14 as not planned - a decision not to merge rather than a fix, so the situation stands: full-size Kimi K3 vision lives on a branch and mainline does not carry it. If you want vision on this model you are building someone's fork.

26382.headline: Same K and V cache type enforced for models with no V cache
26382.why: GLM-5.2's DSA attention has no V cache to quantise, but the flag pair is validated as if it did, so you cannot set the K type independently. Costs memory on the model that has the least to spare.

26894.headline: DFlash drafter fails to bind when the GGUF encodes attention.sliding_window
26894.why: Blocks speculative decoding on exactly the builds that carry a sliding-window key. The target model still runs; you lose the draft head's speedup.

27066.headline: Adaptive-P sampling is broken on Muse Glimmer
27066.why: A sampler, not the model. Pin top-p explicitly and it is a non-issue; listed because the default sampler config is what most launchers use.

27139.headline: Qwen3.8 tool-calling errors resolved by substituting the Qwen3.6 chat template
27139.why: The shipped template mis-renders something in the tool path. A workaround exists and is a single `--chat-template-file`, but until it is fixed the default template is wrong for agent use.

27141.headline: nemotron_h_moe aborts in ggml_ssm_scan during context reservation
27141.why: Fires at context reservation, before any token is generated, and the assertion is in the shared SSM scan rather than a backend - so it is not a CUDA-only report.

27335.headline: Qwen3.8-27B crashes on an M2 Ultra with default settings
27335.why: Confirmed on Darwin arm64 with the Metal backend, and on defaults rather than a tuned command line - the one class of bug that hits you on first run.

27427.headline: A ~50 KB request crashes llama-server with exit 139
27427.why: Filed on Glimmer. 50 KB is an ordinary agent turn once a file or a diff is in the prompt, and the process dies rather than rejecting the request.

27428.headline: draft-mtp roughly halves prompt processing on a multi-GPU layer split
27428.why: Multi-GPU only - a single GPU is fine, so this does not apply to a Mac. Listed because it is the most active MTP thread and the fix will touch the shared path.

27720.headline: gpt-oss malformed Harmony channel headers break tool calls
27720.why: gpt-oss encodes reasoning and tool calls in Harmony channels; a garbled header drops the call. Model specific and parser-side, so it is fixable without touching the weights.

27727.headline: Garbled output from a Qwen3-Coder-Next abliterated GGUF
27727.why: Filed against a community abliterated finetune rather than the base weights, so it may say more about that conversion than about the architecture. Worth knowing before you blame the model.

27741.headline: Feature request: support Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
27741.why: The request thread, still open even though the implementing PR (#27742) merged on 2026-08-27. Worth watching for the follow-up fixes rather than as a blocker; the remaining gap for this model is MLX, not llama.cpp.

32217.headline: feat: add Inkling 2 support (pure model)
32217.why: Open since 2026-11-13. Until it merges llama.cpp has no inkling2 architecture, so the unsloth GGUF quants of Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small cannot load in llama.cpp, LM Studio or any GGUF path. Ollama runs the model on its own runtime today, so this PR is what makes the GGUF quants usable on a Mac.

32187.headline: model: add Inkling 2 (stacked on Inkling 1)
32187.why: Competing PR (2026-11-13) implementing Inkling 2 on top of the Inkling 1 architecture work. Whichever of this or #32217 merges unblocks the GGUF quants.

3293.headline: Qwen4-Exp sparse-attention indexer fails under multi-row batching
3293.why: Fixed on 2026-09-02, but after v0.6.4 shipped and there has been no release since, so a packaged install still fails on any two concurrent requests. It was a shape error from the sparse-attention indexer that only appeared once continuous batching formed a multi-row batch - which is the configuration anyone serving this model would run.

3294.headline: Qwen4-Exp QSA cache: prefix blocks unusable across text and MRoPE turns
3294.why: Four defects in the QSA cache handling vendored in for Qwen4-Exp between v0.6.3rc3 and v0.6.3. Prefix cache reuse is the difference between a fast second turn and paying full prefill again, so this costs exactly what the engine is fastest at.

3300.headline: Loading another Qwen3.5-family VLM permanently breaks qwen4_exp Lightning MTP
3300.why: Fixed on 2026-08-30, and likewise not in a tagged release yet. Loading any other Qwen3.5-family VLM used to kill Lightning MTP for an already-working Flash-Next until restart, silently costing the 2.3x to 2.6x that MTP is worth on generation.

3303.headline: v0.6.4 qwen4-exp performance benchmark returns N/A for some prompt sizes
3303.why: The built-in benchmark intermittently reports nothing at pp16384. A reporting defect rather than an inference one, but it undercuts the numbers you would use to size a machine.

1195.headline: MTP speculative decoding not yet supported for Nemotron-H
1195.why: A feature request. Nemotron 3.5 Lightning ships MTP weights, so this is speed left on the table rather than anything broken.

1783.headline: Continuous batching prefill collapses at exactly two concurrent requests
1783.why: Recovers at higher concurrency, which makes it easy to miss in a benchmark that jumps straight to eight. Two concurrent requests is the most common real case.

1794.headline: Hitting the context wall with Gemma 4
1794.why: Gemma 4 advertises 256k. This is where users find the practical ceiling on a Mac, which is set by KV residency rather than by the model.

1862.headline: MiniMax 3 model-type error
1862.why: The `minimax_m3_vl` model type is not mapped cleanly. Same root cause as the loader failure above, seen from the config side.

1927.headline: GLM-5.2-mxfp4 will not load
1927.why: Filed against 0.4.4. Matters because mxfp4 is the smallest faithful GLM-5.2 build, and the alternative affine quants are larger at the same nominal bit width.

1968.headline: MiniMax-M3 fails to load: 2225 parameters not in model (vision_tower)
1968.why: The released checkpoint is `minimax_m3_vl` - a vision-language model - and the text path rejects the vision tower's tensors instead of skipping them.

2018.headline: OpenAI endpoint returns 500 while the Anthropic endpoint works
2018.why: Both endpoints front the same engine, so a client that speaks Anthropic gets a working server and a client that speaks OpenAI does not. Worth knowing which one your agent uses.

2099.headline: GLM-5.2 loops
2099.why: Repetition loops on the flagship model. A loop burns the context window and the wall clock without producing a turn, which on a metered agent is worse than an error.

2137.headline: GLM-5.2-mxfp4 prefill fell from 160-180 tok/s to 40 tok/s on 0.5.0.dev2
2137.why: Closed as completed in July 2026, with memory also fluctuating between 400 and 520 GB on a 512 GB M3 Ultra. Kept on the list as the reference point for what a healthy GLM-5.2 prefill looks like, and as a reminder that a version bump can cost you a factor of four on this model.

2208.headline: GLM-5.2 cold prefill throttles near the memory ceiling
2208.why: GLM-5.2 leaves very little headroom on any Mac that can hold it, so the adaptive throttle engages in normal use rather than at an extreme.

2216.headline: Legitimate gpt-oss tool calls with explicit to=functions.* are dropped
2216.why: A regression from a stricter channel check. Calls that are correctly formed per the Harmony spec get discarded, so the agent sees a turn with no action.

2252.headline: A broken-load DFlash helper poisons concurrent requests to an unrelated model
2252.why: Cross-contamination between models in the same server, on the Qwen3-Next batched path specifically.

2307.headline: A model-discovery race orphans a loaded engine - 404 GB unreclaimable, restart only
2307.why: Server-wide, not per model. Discovery racing an in-flight load leaks the whole resident model; on a 256 GB machine that is the entire budget gone until you restart.

2469.headline: DeepSeek V4 mxfp4 gather_qmm_blocks crashes on float32 activations
2469.why: MXFP4 is the quantisation DeepSeek actually released, so this is the preferred build rather than a fringe one.

2493.headline: 'Cache signature mismatch' then a severe performance drop on DeepSeek V4
2493.why: The prefix cache silently stops being used, so every turn re-prefills. On long agent conversations that is the difference between seconds and minutes per turn.

2589.headline: Muse Glimmer oQ4e: tool calling broken and decode slow
2589.why: Tool calling is the whole point of Glimmer - it leads MCP Atlas. Traced to a pre-#1839 quantisation, so check which build you pulled before concluding the model is bad.

2590.headline: Scope clarification: MiniMax M3 long-prefill fixes across Q4 and oQ3
2590.why: An open question about which quant tiers the long-prefill fixes cover. Read it before choosing a MiniMax quant, because the answer decides whether long prompts work.

2600.headline: DFlash speculative decoding renders the cache non-functional on Gemma and Glimmer
2600.why: Turning on the draft head disables the prefix cache, so you trade a decode speedup for full re-prefill every turn. On agent workloads that is a net loss.

2604.headline: Glimmer DFlash can end a turn after reasoning without the forced tool call
2604.why: The model finishes its reasoning and stops instead of emitting the call. An agent sees a turn that did nothing, which usually gets retried - so it costs two turns, not one.

2606.headline: Thinking leaks into content when generation is truncated mid-thought
2606.why: A truncated turn returns reasoning as if it were the answer. Downstream that is indistinguishable from the model answering badly, and it corrupts anything that parses the reply.

2641.headline: Glimmer is extremely slow with DFlash on
2641.why: The companion report to the two above: on this family the draft head currently costs more than it saves. Run Glimmer without it.

2691.headline: Request: an oQ4e-mtp quantisation of Qwen3.8-27B
2691.why: oMLX's own quant format with the MTP head merged. Until it exists you are running a generic mlx-community build rather than one tuned for this server.

2747.headline: Qwen3.8-27B single-stream decode regressed 36.5 to 24 tok/s on an M3 Ultra
2747.why: A third of decode throughput, on the model most people will try first, with the MTP path implicated. This is the number to check against before assuming an MLX server beats llama.cpp here.

2786.headline: Gemma 4 performance regressed after 0.6.1
2786.why: A version-pinning matter rather than an architecture one, but it means the newest build is not automatically the right one for this model.

2854.headline: No continuous-batching results published for Qwen3.8 and DFlash2
2854.why: Continuous batching is the reason to run a server instead of the CLI. Unmeasured on this architecture means the concurrency story is unproven, not that it is broken.

2972.headline: Process-global Qwen patches contaminate a resident engine after loading another model
2972.why: Multi-model serving is a headline oMLX feature; this is the cross-contamination it can cause. The second model loads and the first one quietly changes behaviour.

3006.headline: GLM-5.2 prefill far below published figures on an M3 Ultra 512 GB
3006.why: The published 845 tok/s number depends on the native DSA kernels being compiled in. This thread is where you find out whether your install actually has them - the fallback is roughly 30x slower and uses more memory.

3117.headline: Qwen3.8 with the Neural Engine enabled produces zero tokens
3117.why: ANE offload is off by default, so this is an opt-in trap rather than a first-run one - but it is silent, returning an empty completion rather than an error.

3121.headline: DeepSeek V4 Flash decodes at 4-17 tok/s on an M5 Max from residency thrash
3121.why: Closed as completed on 2026-08-28, alongside the v0.6.3 release. It was traced to the bundled mlx keeping a single residency set, so weights faulted instead of staying wired. No post-fix decode figure has been published, so treat the old 4-17 tok/s as historical rather than current - and the other DeepSeek defects on this engine are still open.

2240.headline: Too much memory allocated
2240.why: Over-allocation relative to the model. On a 256 GB machine running a 200 GB model there is no slack to absorb it.

2243.headline: Native MLX tool calling: parser coverage requests
2243.why: Tool-call parsing is per-family, so a model whose format has no parser returns its calls as text. Track this if your model is not in the supported list.

2265.headline: MLX Gemma 4 silently ignores attached images and confabulates a description
2265.why: The GGUF build of the same model handles them. A vision model that invents what it cannot see is the worst available failure mode, and it is engine-specific.

2273.headline: MLX quants shown as having no tool use when they do
2273.why: The capability badge is wrong, so the app steers you away from working tool-calling builds. Cosmetic in code, decision-changing in practice.

2323.headline: MLX engine silently clamps context to 4864 tokens, ignoring all overrides
2323.why: Filed against a hybrid linear-attention model - the Qwen3.8 shape. A silent 4864-token ceiling makes any agent workload fail in a way that looks like the model being stupid rather than the engine being misconfigured.

2324.headline: Catalog entries show 'Invalid Key ID' with no download options
2324.why: A catalogue-side failure rather than an inference one, but the catalogue is how most people get models into this app.

1788.headline: Add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp) model support
1788.why: Open. Until it merges mlx-lm has no qwen4_exp class, so every MLX engine that builds on mlx-lm refuses the weights regardless of which quant you point at it.

1162.headline: Qwen3-Next hybrid cache silently fails, breaking the prompt cache
1162.why: Silent, and it removes prefix reuse - the single biggest win on multi-turn agent traffic. Every MLX server that wraps mlx-lm inherits it, so the model looks fine while every turn re-prefills.

1192.headline: The DeepSeek V4 port thread
1192.why: Where the community port was developed and tested before PR #1233. Useful for finding out what already works in a fork if you do not want to wait for the merge.

1233.headline: PR: DeepSeek V4 model class, still open
1233.why: This is the entire MLX blocker for DeepSeek V4. Until it merges there is no `deepseek_v4` in mlx-lm, so no MLX server that wraps mlx-lm can load the architecture no matter which quant you download.

1242.headline: Error loading mlx-community/gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit
1242.why: The published small-variant quant does not load cleanly.

1281.headline: Request: add DeepSeek V4 to mlx_lm
1281.why: The demand-side thread for the PR above. Useful as a temperature check on whether the port is moving.

1332.headline: DeepSeek-V4 unbounded Metal residency during decode
1332.why: Dies at ~11k decode tokens with metal::malloc resource-limit exceeded. Even once the architecture lands, this has to be fixed before the model is servable.

1335.headline: Tool calls dropped when the tokenizer merges the tool-call start marker
1335.why: The json_tools parser never matches, so the call is returned as plain text. Architecture-independent and specific to agent use.

1352.headline: Gemma 4 with thinking enabled returns only reasoning, content empty
1352.why: The visible reply comes back blank whenever thinking is on.

1401.headline: PR: Add MiniMax-M3 (text backbone) - unmerged
1401.why: The only route to M3 on MLX, open since 2026-08-24. The only route to M3 on MLX.

1404.headline: DeepSeek V4 Flash drifts from Simplified to Traditional Chinese
1404.why: Filed against the mlx-vlm DeepSeek path, which is the only working MLX route today. A quality defect rather than a load failure, and confined to CJK output.

1418.headline: GLM-5.2 fails to load — missing per-layer indexer params
1418.why: The loader expects a DeepSeek-V3.2-style indexer on every layer, but GLM-5.2's IndexShare places them on a subset. mlx-community/GLM-5.2-mxfp4 aborts with 285 missing parameters.

1443.headline: DSA Indexer sparse top-k evicts attention sinks
1443.why: Past index_topk (2048) the indexer drops the attention sinks and decode collapses into repetition — a sharp cliff, not drift. Hits every sparse-attention model: DeepSeek V3.2/V4 and GLM-5.2 both decode through this module.

1446.headline: ArraysCache is not trimmable
1446.why: The structural reason the k=1 cap exists — GDN state layers cannot be rolled back on draft rejection. Same root cause as #730.

1493.headline: Generation hangs at 0% CPU right after prompt processing
1493.why: A wedge, not a slowdown - the server stops doing work with no error.

1572.headline: >300GB models trip the GPU watchdog at load
1572.why: load_model() ends with one mx.eval(model.parameters()), building a single enormous Metal command buffer. At ~390GB it hits kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorTimeout and the error escapes uncaught, hard-aborting the process. GLM-5.2 at 4-bit is 372-475GB.

1573.headline: RotatingKVCache.to_quantized() blocks --kv-bits on sliding-window layers
1573.why: Gemma 4's sliding-window attention cannot use a quantised KV cache.

1662.headline: Models that discard update_and_fetch's return leak one Metal buffer per layer per generation
1662.why: Fixed upstream. #1784 makes decode evaluate cache state periodically and #1790 fixes the unevaluated graph in deepseek specifically; both merged, and this closed 2026-08-27. It was the general form of the DeepSeek V4 residency growth - any model class written that way leaked for the life of the process, aborting at around 11k generated tokens rather than failing on the first run.

2061.headline: Add Inkling 2 model
2061.why: Open since 2026-11-13. Until it merges mlx-lm has no inkling2 class, so the mlx-community Inkling 2 Small MLX quants cannot load through mlx-lm, oMLX or vllm-mlx.

14116.headline: Tiered context length can exhaust VRAM
14116.why: Fixed, closed 2026-09-04. The automatic context sizing could commit more memory than the machine had, and on a Mac that is unified memory, so it took the whole machine rather than just a GPU. Kept listed so the fix is dated.

15813.headline: Metal backend crash on Apple M5: bfloat/half type mismatch
15813.why: An M5-specific crash in the Metal matmul path. If you are buying an M5 machine, this is the one to check is closed before you plan around Ollama on it.

17323.headline: Bare-JSON tool-call models silently drop content generated after the call
17323.why: The call survives and the accompanying text does not. Silent truncation is worse than an error because the agent proceeds on a partial turn.

17569.headline: x/mlxrunner panics importing a plain Qwen3 MLX 4-bit model
17569.why: An index-out-of-range in the MLX runner's dense MLP forward. Importing an ordinary mlx-community checkpoint is a normal thing to want to do.

17638.headline: gpt-oss: HTTP 500 'error parsing tool call' on a call its own model generated
17638.why: The server rejects output produced by the model it shipped. From the agent's side it is a hard failure on a turn that was otherwise correct.

17656.headline: muse-glimmer:30b-mlx is built from nvfp4-dflash layers, not real MLX weights
17656.why: The tag says MLX and the manifest says something else, so you may not be running what you think you are. Worth knowing generally: an Ollama tag is a manifest, not a guarantee about the underlying build.

17776.headline: Qwen3.8-27B MTP variants are 2x slower than non-MTP on Apple Silicon
17776.why: Speculative decoding making decode twice as slow is the opposite of the intent. On this model MTP is the main reason to prefer one engine over another, so a negative result here matters.

17783.headline: gemma4:31b-mlx grows in memory over a session
17783.why: Fixed, closed 2026-09-10. Resident size climbed across a session on the MLX path, which matters most on a machine sized close to the model - the failure arrives after hours rather than at load. Kept listed so the fix is dated.

17878.headline: Embeddings silently return all-zero vectors under sustained load
17878.why: HTTP 200, plausible usage numbers, and useless vectors. Not an LLM path, but it says something about how failures surface here.

360.headline: RFC: a specialised Metal kernel for MLA paged attention
360.why: Until this exists, latent-attention models fall back to MLX SDPA with no Metal kernel - which is why the GLM-4.5 row in the support matrix is flagged as slow and untested.

450.headline: RFC: attention backend dispatch
450.why: Design work on how backends get selected per model. Useful for judging how settled the internals are.

482.headline: Draft-model speculative decoding is net-negative
482.why: Each request re-ingests the full prompt into the draft model, which costs more than the draft saves. Worth knowing before you reach for spec decode here; the built-in MTP path (#610) is the one to watch.

610.headline: Built-in MTP draft heads do not yet work with prefix caching on hybrid GDN
610.why: Qwen3.8 is exactly that shape, and it ships an MTP head. Until this lands you choose between the draft head and the prefix cache rather than having both.

644.headline: Nemotron-H (Mamba-2 + MoE hybrid) paged attention not implemented
644.why: Closed as completed on 2026-09-09 after a long chain of work - hybrid geometry behind a family owner, a state-family routing table, Mamba-2 mixers on paged state, and finally Nemotron-H through the decode pipeline. Kept listed because the fix is nightly-only: the v0.28.0 stable predates it. Before this, such a model loaded, warmed up, reported healthy and then killed EngineCore on the first request.

646.headline: Mixed batches with top_k enabled on some requests crash the Metal sampler
646.why: Fixed. PR #648 normalises disabled top_k rows to vocab_size and merged 2026-08-27, closing this. It mattered because continuous batching puts requests with different sampling parameters in one batch, so it was reachable with ordinary mixed traffic. Kept listed so the fix is dated: you want a build from 2026-08-27 or later.

546.headline: Strict json_schema decode wedges with no token progress
546.why: Over 5-minute hangs on Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B. Structured output is load-bearing for tool arguments.

570.headline: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B dequantize shape mismatch (works in mlx-vlm)
570.why: Same class as mlx-lm #1197: mlx-vlm handles a checkpoint the mlx-lm path does not.

584.headline: Non-loopback requests silently dropped on --host 0.0.0.0
584.why: Deployment blocker: a server on the LAN is reachable only from localhost. Silent — no log, recv-queue 0.

590.headline: Gemma 4 TextModel dispatch, logit_bias API, and MLLM fallback stalls
590.why: Dispatch falls through to qwen3_5 rather than the Gemma path.

619.headline: Hardcoded mx.set_cache_limit(32GB) is not device-scaled
619.why: Filed as an OOM on small Macs, but it cuts the other way here: a hardcoded 32GB ceiling on a 256GB box leaves most of the machine unused.

627.headline: memory_budget_gb never reconciled with the Metal allocation ceiling
627.why: Two allocators with different ideas of the budget. Relevant when hot-swapping checkpoints for A/B runs.

641.headline: MemoryAwarePrefixCache stores caches by reference
641.why: Leaks Metal buffer handles on hybrid models. Compounds every other memory-pressure item at concurrency.

658.headline: Validate Qwen MoE MTP conversion artifacts before decode
658.why: Would catch a broken MTP head at load instead of at generation.

668.headline: DeepSeek V4 Flash unsupported
668.why: ValueError: Model type deepseek_v4 not supported. Open since 2026-08-01, no maintainer reply, no PR — and mlx-lm has no deepseek_v4.py, so the architecture is unimplemented upstream too.

672.headline: Streaming tool calls can end without finish_reason
672.why: Fixed, closed 2026-08-30. It mattered because a streaming tool call that ends without a terminator is exactly the shape that reads as a fabricated turn downstream. Kept listed so the fix is dated.

678.headline: Prefix cache trims RotatingKVCache past its window
678.why: Cross-conversation KV leak and repetition loops. A correctness bug, not a speed bug — one tenant's context bleeding into another's is disqualifying for multi-agent serving.

682.headline: Closing a stream leaves the inner generator and request state open
682.why: Client disconnects are routine in agentic work; leaked request state accumulates.

689.headline: Completion cache can store desynchronized rotating KV state
689.why: Another way the cache serves state that does not match the prompt it is keyed on.

699.headline: DFlash and DSpark draft heads block speculative decoding
699.why: Both are the vendor-shipped draft mechanisms on the models that have one. If neither is wired up, speculative decoding on this engine is limited to what the generic k=1 path gives you.

710.headline: MTP drafting pinned to k=1 on hybrid linear-attention
710.why: Reference CUDA/vLLM deployments run k=3 at ~77% acceptance for a ~66% decode gain. Measured on Qwen3.8-27B / M3 Ultra 256GB: verify forward is 69% of step time, reject and replay 19.3%.

711.headline: --prefill-step-size silently dropped under --continuous-batching
711.why: Prefill chunk size is the main Apple Silicon prefill lever, ignored in exactly the config we would run.

725.headline: PR: GLM-4.7 thinking streams into content, not reasoning_content
725.why: With --reasoning-parser glm4 the entire thinking block lands in content. Non-streaming is unaffected, so it is easy to miss - an agent frontend renders the model's reasoning as the visible reply.

729.headline: PR: honor --prefill-step-size with continuous batching
729.why: Merged 2026-09-04. It was one of two competing fixes for #711; this is the one that landed, making --prefill-step-size actually apply under continuous batching.

730.headline: Prefix-cache reuse silently disabled for hybrid architectures
730.why: #691's all-or-nothing rewind gate rejects every hybrid model: ArraysCache leaves have no .keys and inherit is_trimmable() -> False. Measured on Qwen3.8-27B-8bit — an identical 24k prompt resent back-to-back gives zero speedup on main, versus ~58x before #691. Rejection logs only at DEBUG.

731.headline: PR: make prefix-cache rewind gate aware of non-KV hybrid leaves
731.why: Explicitly Fixes #730, opened 2026-08-25 with the 58x measurement attached. The single event that most changes this plan.

732.headline: PR: surface prefix-cache reuse via usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens
732.why: Observability. Without it there is no way to confirm a hit rate from the API — which is how #730 stayed silent.

987.headline: Support for MiniMax-H3-Image (33B T2I + editing, 6 steps)
987.why: A 33.1B image model that outputs 16 MP in 6 steps cannot load on any engine on this page; mflux is the image engine and this is the request that would unblock it.

top: Maxwell-V1-Flash: 35B/3B-active MoE with 256K context trends on Hugging Face

A new open-weight MoE from the Maxwell Team, trending on Hugging Face: 35B total parameters with only 3B active per token, 256K-token context, 45 transformer layers. Its headline feature is Maxwell Block Sparse Attention, which bounds each KV group's main attention at 4,096 tokens while keeping the full-history KV cache available, and the card claims the MBSA kernel is 6.7x faster than dense GQA at 256K - the economics long-context inference on a Mac has been missing. No MLX or GGUF quant has landed yet, so nothing on Apple silicon can load it today; with 35B total parameters the first 4-bit conversion would be roughly 18 GB resident.
https://huggingface.co/maxwell-model/Maxwell-V1-Flash
Microsoft releases Aion 1.0 Instruct: 2.3B MIT-licensed Windows SLM with 32K context

Microsoft's Windows Applied Sciences Group published Aion 1.0 Instruct, the foundational small language model for the Windows ecosystem: 2.3B parameters, 32K context, eight languages, MIT-licensed, and aimed at on-device document comprehension, summarization and chat. This is the unquantized preview - the card says quantized versions follow, and an optimized Aion paired with a content-moderation model will ship as the Windows OS SLM by the end of January 2027. GGUF is already listed as a supported format, and at 2.3B the model is about 4.6 GB in 16-bit, so it fits comfortably on any Mac once a quant lands.
https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Aion-1.0-Instruct-2.3B
NVIDIA publishes a 4.21B speculative-decoding draft model for Qwen3.8-27B

NVIDIA released an official external speculative-decoding draft for Qwen3.8-27B, the flagship this page tracks: a complete 4.21B model rather than a draft head, sharing the target's tokenizer and proposing blocks of candidate tokens that Qwen3.8-27B verifies by rejection sampling, which cuts decode latency without changing the target's output distribution. The Qwen3.5-4B draft base is Apache 2.0 and the checkpoint ships under the NVIDIA Open Model Agreement. The card officially targets only vLLM on NVIDIA Blackwell under Linux; using it on a Mac would mean vLLM on Metal with the 4.2B draft resident alongside the 27B target, a path the card does not cover and that remains unverified.
https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-4B-Qwen3.8-27B-Draft
Qwen3.8-27B gets a MACaQ 4-bit MLX quant: 18.1 GB, ~3x bf16 decode speed

mlx-community has published a calibrated MXFP4 4-bit (W4A16) quantization of Qwen3.8-27B built with the MACaQ method (arXiv 2611.10649) at 18.1 GB versus 54.7 GB for bf16, licensed Apache-2.0. All 400 decoder linear layers sit at 4.25 bits per weight while embeddings, lm_head and norms stay bf16; it is text-only, with the vision tower not included. It runs on a Mac via mlx-lm with --trust-remote-code using a bundled ~100-line loader that depends only on mlx and mlx-lm, and is reported at about 26-31 tok/s greedy decode on an M5 Max (bf16: about 9 tok/s) with 23.6 GB peak memory. Card measurements: KLD on WikiText-2 of 0.0277 and PPL of 7.1565, better than both the affine 4-bit (KLD 0.0402) and plain mxfp4 (KLD 0.0606) conversions.
https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3.8-27B-MACaQ-W4A16-mlx
Edge0-145B: 145B/10B-active agent MoE posts 86.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and runs on M2 Ultra

Edge0-145B is a 145B-parameter latent sparse MoE agent model - 10.12B active per token, 48 layers, 512 experts per layer (10 routed plus 1 shared active), 256K context, trained natively at 4 bits and built on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next - and it posts 86.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. The NVFP4 build in this repo targets NVIDIA GPUs (23.25 GiB VRAM plus 38.27 GiB host RAM on an RTX 5090 D); for a Mac, the card's speed table lists the Q3_K build on Apple M2 Ultra (Metal) at 755.6-800.3 tok/s prefill, 57.0 tok/s agent decode and 60.9 tok/s chat decode, with 40.81 GiB of Q3_K weights. It is licensed under the edge0-community-model-1.0 terms.
https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Edge0-145B-NVFP4
NVIDIA's Dory 1.0 4B looped reasoning model gets an 8-bit MLX conversion (patched runtime required)

mlx-community has converted NVIDIA's Dory 1.0 4B - a ~4B-parameter looped reasoning model that declares 262,144 positions and a reasoning-mode chat template - to uniform MLX affine 8-bit (group size 64) with the remaining parameters in BF16; model.safetensors is 4.22 GB and the license is openmdw-1.1. The catch is that stock oMLX 0.7.3 lacks the Dory MLX-LM implementation and the relevant MLX-LM PR #1988 was still pending when the conversion was recorded, so the repo's pinned Dory-enabled MLX-LM overlay must be installed before the model loads; trust_remote_code alone does not supply the runtime.
https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-Dory1.0-4B-MLX-8bit
Zyphra releases ZONOS3-Mini: 800M-parameter open TTS, real-time voice cloning on a Mac

Zyphra published ZONOS3-Mini under Apache 2.0: an 800M-parameter text-to-speech model (about 100M active per token, a latent MoE of 64 experts over an 11-layer hybrid backbone of 9 Gated DeltaNet layers and 2 global-attention layers) that speaks 43 languages with 27 built-in voices, clones a voice from a reference clip, and outputs 44.1 kHz audio with a 32K context. On a Mac it runs through MLX-Audio via the mlx-community/ZONOS3-Mini conversion — model, codec and speaker encoder together weigh about 1.4 GB — and the card claims real-time on laptops and phones. Technical report: arXiv 2611.16525.
https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini
Microsoft publishes Aion 1.0, the 2.3B Windows OS small language model, under MIT

Microsoft's Windows Applied Sciences group released Aion 1.0 Instruct, the 2.29B-parameter small language model that will become the Windows OS SLM by the end of January 2027, under an MIT licence. It is a 28-layer hybrid-attention causal LM (21 sliding-window layers at a 2048 window plus 7 full-attention layers, 32K context) trained on an extension of the Phi Silica data and aimed at on-device OS work in eight languages. The unquantized bf16 original is about 4.6 GB, and a 4-bit imatrix GGUF for llama.cpp (AtomicChat) is already published, so the quantised version is roughly a quarter of that and fits comfortably on any Apple silicon Mac.
https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Aion-1.0-Instruct-2.3B
newModels: Microsoft's 2.29B-parameter, MIT-licensed on-device SLM (the future Windows OS model); the bf16 original is about 4.6 GB, and a 4-bit GGUF for llama.cpp has already shipped, so the quantised version runs in roughly a gigabyte or two on any Mac

top: Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights: 2.8T MoE at 1.56 TB in MXFP4, the page's top open model, and no Mac can hold it

Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro is on the page with its full open weights (moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro): a 2.8T-parameter mixture of experts that activates 104B per token, natively multimodal (text plus image), 1M-token context, trained quantization-aware so the published weights are already MXFP4 with MXFP8 activations across 96 shards totalling 1.56 TB. It is the strongest open-weights model tracked here (Artificial Analysis intelligence 46, ahead of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) and is already listed in the Ollama catalogue. The cost on a Mac is the point: 1.56 TB of weights is about three times the 512 GB of the largest Mac Studio, so no Mac can load the full model, and the card's own deployment path is vLLM, SGLang or TokenSpeed on multi-GPU servers. The Kimi K3.1 Pro licence permits use, fine-tuning and redistribution, with a separate agreement required for model-as-a-service operators above $20M annual revenue and attribution required for products above 100M monthly users.
https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro
Tencent Hy4 flash weights ship: 220B MoE with 12B active and a KV cache 1/24 the size of Hy3's

Tencent announced Hy4 flash on November 16 and the open weights landed on Hugging Face on November 17 (tencent/Hy4-flash, plus an FP8 variant and the pre-trained base): a 220B-parameter mixture of experts, 155.5B backbone plus a 63.5B n-gram Engram table, that activates only 12B parameters per token, takes text and images natively and runs a 1M-token context. Everything is built for cost: hybrid sparse (up to 2,048-token selection) plus 512-token sliding-window attention cuts the KV cache to 1/24 of Hy3's and 1/6 of Hy4's, LatentMoE routes 16 of 512 experts in a compressed latent space, and a built-in 0.85B DFly2 drafter does speculative decoding with zero extra KV memory. Tencent reports a WorkIndex score of 42.1, above Hy4 preview's 39.7, at 1/13 the cost per task, and past 150 tok/s decoding with 4-bit quantization and megakernels. On a Mac, the 220B of weights is roughly 110 GB at 4-bit, which is 256 GB or 512 GB Mac Studio territory on paper, but the card ships vLLM and SGLang (GPU) deployment only and whether llama.cpp or mlx-lm can load the new LatentMoE/Engram architecture is still open, so it is not runnable on Apple silicon today. It carries the custom Tencent Hy License.
https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-flash
Qwen3.8-27B gets a MACaQ MXFP4 MLX quant: 18.1 GB, 26-31 tok/s on an M5 Max

mlx-community published a new 4-bit MLX build of Qwen3.8-27B made with MACaQ, a calibrated MXFP4 post-training quantization (arXiv 2611.10649): MXFP4 weights with bf16 activations (W4A16), all 400 decoder linear layers at 4.25 bits per weight, 18.1 GB against 54.7 GB for the bf16 checkpoint, Apache-2.0 like the base model. Measured against bf16 on the same harness it holds 92.6-92.9% top-1 token agreement and beats both of mlx-lm's own 4-bit conversions on KL divergence and perplexity. The card reports 26-31 tok/s greedy decode on an M5 Max, about three times the roughly 9 tok/s of bf16, with 23.6 GB peak memory, which fits a 32 GB Mac. It runs through mlx-lm with a bundled roughly 100-line loader (macaq_model.py) via trust_remote_code; a plain mxfp4 load deliberately fails because it would drop the per-channel scale and Hadamard rotation. It is text-only: the base model's vision tower is not included.
https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3.8-27B-MACaQ-W4A16-mlx
newModels: SenseNova's looped multimodal model, released November 17 under Apache-2.0: about 9B parameters (14.6B inference-equivalent) that re-run a shared 24-layer block twice, giving 56 decoder-layer executions from 32 physical layers, with hybrid linear/full attention and a 512K context. Text and image in, text out; it targets agentic, coding and data-analysis work and matches Qwen3.8-27B on AIDABench (65.31 vs 65.01) at a fraction of the memory. An official AWQ 4-bit build ships on launch day and the card puts multimodal inference at a 256K context with an 8-bit KV cache at about 15 GiB, comfortable on a 32 GB Mac; the 4-bit checkpoint itself is only about 4.7 GB, so shorter contexts run on 16 GB machines. Fourteen community quantizations for llama.cpp and LM Studio are already up.

top: Qwen-Image-2.1: 7.1B single-stream DiT that unifies text-to-image and editing

Qwen open-sourced the compact successor to the 20B Qwen-Image: a 7.1B single-stream DiT (32 layers) that does text-to-image and editing in one checkpoint, under the Qwen Research License rather than Apache. It takes up to 10 reference images, accepts local edits as circles, painted annotations or masks, and natively emits transparent RGBA output at up to 2752 px on the long edge (1:1 through 16:9). The card's quick start is bfloat16 - the 7B DiT is about 14 GB of weights plus the text encoder - and documents a CPU-offload path for smaller machines; the page tracks mflux as the best-fit engine.
https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1
Tencent's DSpine draft model: 2.7-3.8x decode speedups for Qwen3.8-27B, SGLang-only for now

DSpine (arXiv 2609.36173) is a five-layer 2.0B-parameter draft model - block size 16, 8,192-token sliding window, Apache-2.0, about 4 GB on disk - that lets SGLang draft 16 tokens in parallel for Qwen3.8-27B. In the card's BF16 runs it raises end-to-end throughput to 2.7-3.8x autoregressive decoding (up to 840 tok/s on WorkBuddy Web with xhigh reasoning) and beats the DFlash2 draft on acceptance length in every table. The documented runtime is GPU SGLang with FlashAttention-3, Triton and FlashInfer, and an open llama.cpp PR (#31941, since Nov 9) is working on draft support - unmerged, so today it is a speed reference for the page's flagship, not a Mac download.
https://huggingface.co/tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16
GLM-Tandem: GLM-5.3-Flash on two Mac Studios, tensor-parallel, at about 140 tokens/s

A new repo, icryo/GLM-Tandem, is a recipe for serving GLM-5.3-Flash across two Mac Studios (M5 Ultra, 256 GB each) joined by Thunderbolt 5 RDMA, split tensor-parallel, on top of oMLX's cluster loader and stock mlx_lm.server with an OpenAI-style API. The checkpoint is a uniform 4-bit (group 64) GLM-5.3-Flash with its MTP draft head, 169 GiB, half on each machine. Fresh prose decodes at 141-146 tok/s for one request (speculative decoding with the model's own MTP head accepts about 77-79% of drafts), 223 tok/s total across 8 concurrent requests, and 122 tok/s at 80-200k context; prompt processing runs at about 2,080 tok/s. The cost is the top of the current lineup - two 256 GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios - and the recipe is tied to oMLX 0.8.0rc1, which it patches at load time; requests with very different context lengths decoded together fall to about 5 tok/s each.
https://github.com/icryo/GLM-Tandem
InternLM ships Sage-S2.1: a 753B flagship and a 321B Flash, MIT-licensed

The internlm org has published the Sage-S2.1 family on Hugging Face: a 753B-parameter flagship and a 321.3B 'Flash' variant first published 2026-11-15, each with FP8 and BF16 checkpoints, MIT-licensed. The model card is empty - no architecture, context length or benchmarks - so nothing on the page can rank it yet. What it costs to run: the smallest published checkpoint of the 321B Flash is the FP8 build, roughly one byte per weight, around 320 GB, which is 512 GB Mac Studio territory at best and no MLX or GGUF quant is out yet; the 753B flagship is beyond any single Mac at the published precision.
https://huggingface.co/internlm/Sage-S2.1-Flash
Zyphra's ZONOS3-Mini: open TTS with 100M active parameters and an MLX server for Apple silicon

ZONOS3-Mini is Zyphra's compact open-source text-to-speech model: 800M parameters total, about 100M active per token (latent MoE, 64 experts, top-2 routing), 44.1 kHz audio, 43 languages, voice cloning from a reference clip of up to 60 seconds, word-level control of emotion, pace and delivery, and up to 10 minutes per generation, under Apache 2.0 with a technical report (arXiv 2611.16525). It claims real time on phones and laptops, and the repo ships the runtimes to match: a CUDA server, an MLX server for Apple silicon, a C++/ggml server that can use Metal, and a WebGPU in-browser build. Within the last 36 hours Zyphra also published ZAC-1-hf, the native Transformers port of its ZAC-1 codec (15 Hz frames, 10 codebooks of 4,096 entries, causal multi-resolution iSTFT decoder): encoder and decoder in one float32 checkpoint of about 2B parameters (~8 GB), Apache-2.0, loadable with plain AutoModel on a Mac.
https://huggingface.co/Zyphra/ZAC-1-hf
newModels: InternLM's 321.3B-parameter Flash variant of the new Sage-S2.1 family (753B flagship alongside, FP8 and BF16 checkpoints of each), MIT-licensed, first published 2026-11-15. No MLX or GGUF quant is out yet: the smallest published checkpoint is FP8 at roughly one byte per weight (~320 GB), so expect 512 GB Mac Studio territory at best, and the card still carries no architecture or benchmarks.

top: Page now tracks MiniMax-H3-Image: 16 MP native, 33.1B DiT, no Mac engine can load it yet

MiniMax-H3-Image is the biggest image model on the page and the only one that outputs 16 MP natively: 4096x4096 up to 6272x2688 directly with no upscaler, distilled to 6 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance, with text-to-image and editing of up to 16 reference images unified in one checkpoint. The diffusion transformer is 33.1B parameters in BF16 (66.28 GB for transformer/, 2.34 GB for the VAE) and it loads a 66.7 GB Qwen3-VL text encoder from the MiniMax-H3 repo, so a full local copy is roughly 135 GB. It ships under MiniMax's community license agreement rather than a standard open licence. The card's deployment targets are all GPU frameworks (SGLang, vLLM-Omni, diffusers, LightX2V, ComfyUI, on H200, RTX PRO 6000 and MI350X); no engine on the page can load it yet, so the entry is a tracking card for the gap, not a working Mac recipe.
https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image
Leech-lattice quantization reaches Qwen3 at 2.7 bits per weight: better than IQ2_S on quality, slower, with a Metal build for Mac

A Rust runtime (Apache-2.0, github.com/pjmalandrino/llvq) implements Qualcomm's Leech-lattice vector quantization and publishes Qwen3-4B, 8B and 14B sealed at 2.70-2.73 bits per parameter: 1.38, 2.76 and 5.04 GB of weights, with measured MMLU of 63.4, 69.6 and 75.7 and WikiText-2 perplexity of 12.58, 9.71 and 8.44 on one L40S. The author reports +9.1, +4.1 and +2.9 MMLU points over llama.cpp's IQ2_S calibrated to the same bits, at the cost of speed: IQ2_S decodes 60, 64 and 34 tok/s faster than LLVQ's 113.8, 95.0 and 57.2 tok/s. llama.cpp cannot read the custom format; the runtime speaks the Ollama and OpenAI APIs, CUDA is the primary backend, and the repo builds with a Metal feature for Mac, though no Mac numbers have been published. So a 14B in 5 GB is a candidate for a 16 GB Mac on paper, not in practice.
https://github.com/pjmalandrino/llvq
mlx-community ships an 8-bit MLX build of NVIDIA's Dory 1.0 4B looped reasoning model - with a patched-runtime catch

mlx-community converted NVIDIA's Dory 1.0 4B - a looped reasoning model with about 3.975B parameters, a declared 262k context, and weights shared across two recurrent loops by default - to uniform MLX affine 8-bit with group size 64 (remainder BF16), roughly 4 GB of weights. It is the first MLX path to the model, but stock mlx-lm 0.7.3 has no Dory model class and the upstream PR (#1988) is still pending, so the card ships pinned runtime patches and a tokenizer fallback instead of a drop-in install. The converter's local GPQA-Diamond run scored 69.7% at 2 loops and 75.3% at 4 loops against NVIDIA's reported 72.4% and 72.2% for the BF16 model, and the card itself says the methods were not matched, so that is not a quantization claim. The model is governed by NVIDIA's OpenMDW-1.1 agreement, not a standard open licence.
https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-Dory1.0-4B-MLX-8bit
